aria: Animated recap of the Spurs' 122 to 96 road win at Phoenix: Victor Wembanyama's 3-pointer with 31 seconds left in the third quarter, quarter-by-quarter scoring, his 40 points, 11 rebounds and 9 blocks in 25 minutes, the top scorers, how the Spurs won, and the next game at Chicago.
notes: Box score from the Spurs' 122–96 road win over the Phoenix Suns on Nov 9, 2026, from StatMuse's full box score, with game details from the AP (via The Sports Leader), Yahoo Sports, KYMA, Al Jazeera, Land of Basketball and VAVEL. All 122 Spurs points and all 96 Suns points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores add up to both totals (61–46 at the half, matching the AP). Wembanyama's 9 blocks are from the StatMuse box score and match Yahoo Sports, KYMA and Land of Basketball; the AP and Al Jazeera say eight, so the box score is used. The league stats feed wasn't available for this recap, so records come from the site's standings through Nov 8 plus Monday's results (San Antonio 9–2, matching Yahoo Sports; Chicago 1–8).

Biggest lead: San Antonio's 34, at 104–70 after Wembanyama's running dunk with 9:34 left (AP). Phoenix's last lead was 25–24 on Devin Booker's three with 1:41 left in the first quarter (AP); the sources don't give Phoenix's biggest lead, so the reel doesn't show one. Free-throw percentages are from the box score (19 of 25 and 17 of 19). The Sleepy Floyd note (the only player since 1980–81 to score 40 in fewer minutes) is from Yahoo Sports. The Spurs play at Chicago on Wednesday at 8:00 PM ET (FanDuel Research's Spurs schedule).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Victor Wembanyama's 3-pointer with 31 seconds left in the third quarter, which made it 93–68 (AP); the line score confirms 93–68 after three. The recaps don't describe how he got the shot, so it is drawn as the template's plain pull-up. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the San Antonio Spurs or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Wembanyama’s listed 7-foot-4 and 235 pounds (RealGM), with arms scaled to his reported 8-foot wingspan (Sportskeeda), in the Spurs' road kit with his approved look. His No. 1 is from RealGM. It is an original silhouette with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
